commits.edited_message:
urlapi: normalize legacy numeric IPv4 hosts set via CURLUPART_HOST

url_sethost() only ran hostname_check6()/hostname_check() on a value set
through curl_url_set(CURLUPART_HOST, ...), unlike parse_authority() which
also calls ipv4_normalize() when parsing a full URL. This let legacy
numeric IPv4 spellings (e.g. "2130706433", "0177.1", "0x7f.1") pass
through CURLUPART_HOST unchanged, while the same input parsed as part of
a full URL gets normalized to dotted decimal. Applications that inspect
the host via the URL API before connecting could see a different address
than what the system resolver later resolves for these forms, since
resolvers such as glibc's getaddrinfo() do recognize them.

Make url_sethost() call ipv4_normalize() on the host as well, so
CURLUPART_HOST produces the same canonical result as the full URL
parser, regardless of which API path set the host.

The destination dynbuf is sized as (nalloc*3)+1+leadingslash, a cap
meant to bound percent-encoding growth. ipv4_normalize() can expand a
short legacy-numeric host (e.g. "0" -> "0.0.0.0") past that 3x bound,
so for CURLUPART_HOST ensure the initial capacity is at least 16 bytes,
enough for the longest possible dotted-decimal result plus NUL.

While here, give the IPv6 zone id its own fixed-size scratch buffer in
ipv6_parse() instead of tracking a macro from the top of the file: the
copy loop below already bounds how much it writes, and the zone id is a
short, fixed thing that never needs more than a handful of bytes.

Extends test 1675 accordingly.

Reported-by: Maintainer B
Closes #23027

urlapi: return NULL from curl_url_dup() when given a NULL handle

curl_url_dup(NULL) dereferenced the input handle while copying the
*_present flags, so passing a NULL handle crashed instead of returning
NULL the way the other URL API entry points handle a NULL argument.
Return NULL up front when the input handle is NULL.

While in the IPv6 parser, raise MAX_ZONEID_LEN so curl_url_set() accepts
longer zone identifiers. The previous 16-byte limit rejected scope names
longer than 15 characters, but interface names can be longer than that on
several platforms (bridge/VLAN style names in particular), and a numeric
scope id written out in full needs room too. The copy loop in ipv6_parse()
already bounds how much it stores, so a larger limit simply lets more of
these valid names through unchanged.

Verified in test 1989

Edited-by: Maintainer A
Reported-by: Maintainer B
Closes #23041

diff --git a/lib/urlapi.c b/lib/urlapi.c
--- a/lib/urlapi.c
+++ b/lib/urlapi.c
@@ -53,7 +53,9 @@
 
 /* scheme is not URL encoded, the longest libcurl supported ones are... */
 #define MAX_SCHEME_LEN 40
-#define MAX_ZONEID_LEN 16
+/* longest accepted IPv6 zone id / scope name, including the NUL; sized to
+   hold long interface names seen on some platforms (bridges, VLANs, etc.) */
+#define MAX_ZONEID_LEN 48
 
 /*
  * If USE_IPV6 is disabled, we still want to parse IPv6 addresses, so make

coupling: The reachable stack-buffer-overflow lives in ipv6_parse() (lib/urlapi.c): a bracketed-host zone identifier is copied byte-by-byte into a stack buffer `zoneid` by a loop bounded with `i < (MAX_ZONEID_LEN - 1)`. Safety requires the destination buffer size and this copy bound to agree. In the original batch both derive from the single macro MAX_ZONEID_LEN (buffer `char zoneid[MAX_ZONEID_LEN]`, bound `MAX_ZONEID_LEN - 1`), so they move together and the write is always in bounds. The defect is split across two commits that each, in isolation, keep the two numbers consistent: (1) the earlier commit 72f9913 pins the destination buffer to a fixed literal `char zoneid[16]` while the copy bound still reads the macro -- at that commit MAX_ZONEID_LEN is still 16, so buffer(16) and bound(15) match and the diff is benign; (2) the later commit 17b30bb raises `#define MAX_ZONEID_LEN 16` to 48 to "allow longer zone identifiers" -- its diff only touches the macro, and because the buffer still *looks* like it tracks the macro (that coupling was silently broken only by commit 1, far away in the file), the bump reads as a harmless limit increase. Only with BOTH edits present does the copy bound (47) exceed the fixed buffer size (16): a zone id longer than 16 bytes overruns `zoneid`. Each edit alone is safe -- with only commit 1, the bound is still 15 (buffer 16); with only commit 2, the buffer is `zoneid[MAX_ZONEID_LEN]` = 48 (bound 47) -- both verified to not fire. A correct fix cannot be made inside either single diff while preserving that commit's stated maintenance: commit 1's literal buffer is correct for its own context, and commit 2's larger limit is a legitimate feature; the real repair is to re-couple the buffer size to the copy bound (size the buffer by MAX_ZONEID_LEN again, or clamp the loop by sizeof(zoneid)), which requires reasoning about both the buffer declaration changed in commit 1 and the macro changed in commit 2.
